findings.cross_file_justification: floor.yaml declares 16 fence:FR-SZ* and fence:FR-1.2b ids as floor guards; all of them are implemented by regexes in block-destructive-bash.sh (diff-touched), which is absent from floor_files. tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/run-corpus.sh (diff-touched, truncated) is also unpinned.
findings.description: The floor is documented as 'the set of guards ... no profile, knob or cycle task may weaken', and floor-snapshot.bats enforces byte-identity only for the paths listed under floor_files. The script that implements the majority of floor guards (block-destructive-bash.sh) and the corpus runner that exercises them are not listed. Only the corpus JSONL rows for FR-1.2b and FR-SZ* are pinned. A cycle task can therefore loosen an FR-SZ regex, or change how run-corpus.sh evaluates expected blocks, without tripping the floor snapshot, as long as the corpus rows themselves are untouched.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended cycle edits a floor fence regex (e.g. the _sz_file or _c2_file alternation) so a protected path no longer matches; floor-snapshot passes because floor_files is unchanged; the System-Zone write guard is silently weakened while the register still reports the guard as floor: true.
findings.suggested_fix: Add .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh and tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/run-corpus.sh to floor_files (or pin a sha256 of the FR-SZ*/FR-1.2b regex block via a dedicated bats test), and have guard-origins.bats assert that every floor: true fence row's implementing file is itself floor-pinned.

findings.cross_file_justification: guard-origins.yaml (diff-added) row policy:permission-deny-list says the policy covers 'the permission deny rules (settings.json deny list and the credential template)' but points script at .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json, which is the only path floor.yaml pins.
findings.description: The floor pins .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json, which per the policy row's own note is the template, while the live deny list that Claude Code actually enforces lives in .claude/settings.json (also the source of hook registrations). .claude/settings.json is not in floor_files. The floor therefore guarantees the template cannot drift but says nothing about the enforcing configuration, so a deny rule or a hook registration can be removed from settings.json without failing floor-snapshot.bats.
findings.failure_mode: A cycle removes a deny entry or unregisters block-destructive-bash.sh from .claude/settings.json; the floor snapshot still passes because only the template is pinned; policy:permission-deny-list remains marked floor: true in the register.
findings.suggested_fix: Add .claude/settings.json to floor_files (or pin its permissions.deny array and hooks.PreToolUse registrations via a targeted bats assertion), and update the policy row's script field to reference the enforcing file.

findings.description: The implementing-tasks skill's app-zone declaration is widened from read to read-write. This is consistent with /implement being the sanctioned place for app writes, but it is a permission widening landed inside a large, mostly unrelated diff (guard register, evals, templates) with no commit-level rationale, and the GLOSSARY in the same diff still defines the App zone as 'needs confirmation before a write'. If any tooling (validate-skill-capabilities.sh, zone-write-guard, implement-gate) consults the skill's zones: block, the confirmation step for app writes may no longer be requested while implementing.
findings.failure_mode: Future reviewers treat the zones: block as the source of truth for app-write mediation; the implement gate is already advisory-only, so app writes under /implement proceed with no confirmation and no record of why the declaration changed.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the rationale in the skill or the decision ledger, confirm implement-gate.sh and zone-write-guard.sh do not key off this field (or that they intentionally allow it), and keep the GLOSSARY zone definition consistent with the declared behaviour.

findings.description: Every audit row written by the fence (block, allow-override, bypass, allow-marker) is now tagged replay: true whenever the environment variable LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY equals 1. There is no check that a replay is actually in progress (e.g. that the hook was invoked by run-corpus.sh or that stdin is a corpus fixture). Since guard-yield.sh presumably excludes replay rows from the 30-day real-block totals, anything that sets this variable in the harness environment (a settings env block, a shell profile, a CI job) causes real blocks and real overrides to disappear from the yield while still being written to the log.
findings.failure_mode: LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 leaks into an interactive or unattended session; the model's blocked destructive commands and audited overrides are all tagged replay and are filtered out of the Guards status line and the host yield, hiding guard activity from the operator.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the replay flag to the corpus runner: have run-corpus.sh pass an explicit marker (e.g. a nonce file under a temp dir, or a dedicated --replay arg through the hook-guard wrapper) and have emit_block require that marker rather than a bare env var; alternatively have guard-yield.sh report replay-tagged counts separately so they are never silently dropped.
